scope: J035 from-scratch consistency and self-adjusting computation

sources.subject: Self-Adjusting Computation PhD thesis
locators: Chapter 1, pp. 3-4: correctness described as semantic equivalence of change propagation and from-scratch execution
Chapter 4, pp. 35-36: dynamic dependence graph and change propagation
Chapter 5, pp. 37-39: memoized DDGs, side effects, shallow identity, and reuse adjusted by change propagation
Chapter 11, discussion around the factorial example: obsolete reads must be deleted because re-evaluation can diverge or raise exceptions despite being absent from a fresh run
sources.role: original mechanism, correctness criterion, performance separation, and a concrete semantic failure caused by stale trace execution

sources.subject: Adaptive Functional Programming
locators: Abstract: DDG-based adaptation and formal AFL correctness
Section 4.5: change propagation re-executes affected reads in execution order
discussion around Fig. 7: contained obsolete reads are deleted because retaining them can change results, diverge, or raise exceptions
sources.role: typed functional formulation and precise change-propagation correctness discipline

sources.subject: Imperative Self-Adjusting Computation
sources.role: extension from write-once/pure modifiables to multiple writes and cyclic stores; proves observational equivalence of change propagation and from-scratch execution inside SAIL

sources.subject: A Consistent Semantics of Self-Adjusting Computation
sources.role: memoizing change-propagation semantics; consistency for nondeterministic reuse choices and correctness compatibility with purely functional programming, with a machine-checked Twelf proof

sources.subject: Efficient Parallel Self-Adjusting Computation
sources.role: later evidence that correctness machinery and update-efficiency analysis remain separate: not every algorithm/update has low change-propagation cost

sources.subject: Anneal current design authority
sources.role: authoritative success semantics, explicit trust, source/model justification, and deliberate non-decisions against which the literature is applied
